With a minimal target, FC2 immediately forces the predecessor fiber to be downward closed, and the converse uses the same target as FC2 witness. Substituting this normal form into the source's exact Lemma 5.8 definitions gives the displayed box and diamond formulas. The frozen checker was read and independently exhausts all labelled posets through four points, all relations through three points, and all downset modal evaluations in its stated finite range; the infinite theorem is the direct symbolic argument.

final_claim: For any involutive Fischer-Servi frame \((X,\le,R)\), every \(R\)-target is minimal and, for each minimal world \(m\), the predecessor fiber \(D_m=\{x:xRm\}\) is a downset; conversely every family of such downsets defines an IFS relation. Therefore a finite poset \(P\) supports exactly \(|\operatorname{Dn}(P)|^{|\operatorname{Min}(P)|}\) labelled IFS relations, and the two primitive modal operators have the stated formulas through the minimal-world trace.
limitations: The count is labelled on a fixed finite poset, not up to isomorphism.
The primitive modalities factor through the minimal trace, but the full Heyting algebra does not.
No classification of represented modal algebras up to isomorphism is claimed.
